messages.subject: VCOV is not positive definite

Hi, 

I am conducting a gender invariance with a sample size of 428 Females and 186 Males using this code: 

```{r}
perci_model4c <- '
        N_SUB =~ PERCI_1 + PERCI_5 + PERCI_9 + PERCI_13 
        N_INH =~ PERCI_3 + PERCI_7 + PERCI_11 + PERCI_15
        N_ACT =~ PERCI_2 + PERCI_6 + PERCI_10 + PERCI_14 
        N_TOL =~ PERCI_4 + PERCI_8 + PERCI_12 + PERCI_16

        P_ACT =~ PERCI_19 + PERCI_23 + PERCI_27 + PERCI_31
        P_TOL =~ PERCI_20 + PERCI_24 + PERCI_28 + PERCI_32

       N_REG =~ N_SUB + N_INH + N_ACT + N_TOL 
       P_REG =~ P_SUB + P_INH + P_ACT + P_TOL'

perci.gender.scalar <- cfa(perci_model4c,
                           data = final_data_au,
                           estimator = "MLM",
                           group = "gender",      
                           group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
                           meanstructure = TRUE,
                           std.lv = FALSE)
```

messages.subject: Re: VCOV is not positive definite
parts:
a positive not definite matrix means your model is NOT admissible and should not be reported.
You need to fix the model so that there is no negative error variances.
if the 95%CI for N_TOL had included zero you could fix it to a small positive value (.005) but that is not the case here.
i would treat this model as wrong and try to fix it.
this paper has some useful ideas. Chen, F., Bollen, K. A., Paxton, P., Curran, P. J., & Kirby, J. B. (2001). Improper solutions in structural equation models: Causes, consequences, and strategies. Sociological Methods & Research, 29(4), 468-508. doi:doi:10.1177/0049124101029004003

Gavin,

Respectfullly, I disagree with your read here. The warning is that the VCV does not appear to be positive definite, with a very small eigenvalue, but none that is clearly negative..

The negative value Joan cited for N_TOL is its intercept, not its variance, which is of course permissible, and not relevant to the positive-definite issue (I also misread that at first glance). I think Joan can proceed.

Pat
On Mon, Sep 21, 2020 at 4:53 PM Prof. Gavin Brown <gbr...@aucklanduni.ac.nz> wrote:

a positive not definite matrix means your model is NOT admissible and should not be reported.
You need to fix the model so that there is no negative error variances.
if the 95%CI for N_TOL had included zero you could fix it to a small positive value (.005) but that is not the case here.
i would treat this model as wrong and try to fix it.
this paper has some useful ideas. Chen, F., Bollen, K. A., Paxton, P., Curran, P. J., & Kirby, J. B. (2001). Improper solutions in structural equation models: Causes, consequences, and strategies. Sociological Methods & Research, 29(4), 468-508. doi:doi:10.1177/0049124101029004003
